speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: As recently as earlier this week, the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) released data that showed that inflation was indeed cooling.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: But the cost-of-living anxieties have far from abated.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: We hear this in the voices of our residents.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: In particular, there are two groups that we hear it quite loudly from: seniors who have retired many years ago as well as households with lower incomes.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: To that end, I have three supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: The first, does the Ministry of Finance (MOF) look beyond hard data into sentiments and anxieties of the population when it comes to cost of living?

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: The second, beyond the aggregate-level data, does MOF or does the Government look at specific target groups that are more vulnerable?

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: And my third, if the answers to the first two questions are yes, would the Government then consider additional forms of support in the coming year, even when inflation cools?

speaker: Mr Shawn Loh (Jalan Besar)
text: For example, building on the success of the SG60 vouchers, would we consider distributing vouchers to a more targeted subset, specifically, the Pioneer Generation as well as blue Community Health Assist Scheme (CHAS) cardholders, as an example?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Essentially, what we do is we look at the circumstances, we look at the different groups, we also look at specific target groups, if needed.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, the first question was whether MOF looks beyond hard data into sentiments and anxiety.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And really, the answer would be to address what is causing that anxiety or that concern.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Then, the second, do we look at target groups?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And if the Member looks at the various measures, the Member will see that some are targeted at seniors, some are targeted at the lower-income.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: We introduced climate vouchers, initially, for Housing and Development Board dwellers and then, extended it to private housing.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there are different funding for different purposes.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: Sometimes you look at the demographic group, but sometimes you also look at the social purpose.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: For example, you may need to provide support for childcare.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there is a whole range that we look at.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: And will we consider additional forms of support?

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The Member cited SG60 vouchers and targeted subsets.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: The SG60 vouchers were because this is our SG60 year.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: In deciding what to give to mark or commemorate SG60, we thought it would be helpful to give the vouchers because it would help with cost of living but it also gave people options with what to do with it.

speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
text: So, there is a whole range that we will take into account, including the economic situation.
